items.headline: SovAI and BAM Energy sign MOU for Pearl-powered AI compute campuses
items.what_happened: On November 12, 2026 SovAI, which designs behind-the-meter AI compute campuses, and BAM Energy, the Houston developer of the Pearl reactor, announced a memorandum of understanding. BAM describes the Pearl as a factory-built, sealed microreactor of about 7 to 10 MWe that runs on natural uranium with heavy-water moderation, so it needs no enrichment or HALEU. The companies will co-develop a reference design that puts four Pearl modules on one steam plant, about 40 MWe gross. BridgePower Nuclear, BAM's joint venture with USP&E, would run the campuses on interim gas generation until the Pearl is ready.
items.why_it_matters: It is a new 7-10 MWe design that avoids HALEU, the fuel most US microreactors are waiting on. It is also very early: no NRC application has been filed, pre-application talks wait on site control, no campus site is named, and the 2028 first-operation date is a target.
items.binding_note: The release says the MOU is non-binding except as to confidentiality, publicity and non-circumvention; projects remain subject to definitive agreements, site control, financing and licensing.

items.headline: Research Council of Norway funds Emerald's 5 MWe maritime reactor pilot
items.what_happened: Emerald Nuclear's Norwegian subsidiary leads MarNuPS, a maritime nuclear propulsion pilot that would pair its 5 MWe Gem microreactor with shipboard power, storage and control systems. The Research Council of Norway awarded NOK 20 million (about USD 2 million) in initial funding. The partners are also putting in substantial money of their own; Stage 1 alone is estimated at about NOK 150 million.
items.why_it_matters: A 5 MWe unit sits inside the 1-20 MW band, but this is an early research grant for a ship-based pilot, not a supply order. The reactor has not been built, so a land buyer should read it as a sign of maritime interest rather than a delivery date.
items.binding_note: A research-council grant award. The sources do not describe a signed grant agreement, delivery terms or a firm build schedule.
